notes: The Leonardo catalogue entry lists no ports; I used the names 5V, GND and 4 for the header pins the wires go to.
The breadboard is drawn flipped compared with the catalogue naming. Rows a-e (bank 't') are the lower half in the image, and the rails next to them are tp/tn. Bank 'b' is rows f-j.
The text says to attach the button to 5V, but the circuit image shows a red wire from the button's right column to the + rail, which the long red wire feeds from 5V. I followed the image.

The button straddles the centre gap in columns 6 and 8. Only its lower legs are visible, so I assumed the upper legs sit in the matching columns in row f. I assigned the pushbutton ports 1.l, 1.r, 2.l and 2.r to those four holes by assumption.
The blue wire from pin 4 ends at column 6, row c. The 10k pull-down resistor runs from column 6, row a, to the ground (-) rail, so pin 4 is pulled to ground.
Rail hole numbers (tn.1, tp.2, tn.5, tp.6) are estimated from the picture.
The schematic labels the signal pin as 2, but the text and the circuit image use pin 4. I used pin 4.
